about.title: A New Zealand company for applied deep technology.
about.intro: We connect artificial intelligence, data, software and engineering to create responsible technology with measurable real-world value.
about.storyTitle: From complex ideas to useful systems.
storyParagraphs: IndustrialOrigami.AI was established to bridge advanced research and practical commercial technology.
The company is developing an intelligent robotic hand while building wider capability in agentic and generative AI, data science, software engineering, CAD and intelligent automation.
Our method is evidence-led: understand the problem, build a focused prototype, measure performance, learn from users and scale only when the technical and commercial case is credible.

roboticHandResearch.researchTitle: The research gap and how we address it
gapParagraphs: Most robotic grippers are designed for a known object and task. Hands that adapt to varied objects are mechanically complex, need many sensors and are difficult to control reliably.
Our question is how much adaptability can be achieved with a small, modular hand before cost, complexity and control effort outweigh the benefit.
methods: Human hand motion capture to understand joint relationships and grasp types
Simulation and CAD of a two-finger and thumb demonstrator before building
Force, position and tactile sensing on each joint
Layered control: vision and grasp policy on an edge computer, deterministic motor loops on a real-time controller
Staged tests at joint, finger and hand level against a defined object set
roboticHandResearch.baselineNote: These are planning targets for the first demonstrator. None has been validated yet.
baseline: Demonstrator scope: two fingers and a thumb
Motor control loops at about 1 kHz
Vision and grasp policy at about 30 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson edge computer
Operation in a guarded laboratory test cell
notYet: Grasp success across a defined object set
outputs: Design notes for each validated sub-system
roboticHandResearch.outputsNote: Subject to partner and intellectual-property agreements.
roboticHandResearch.safety: All testing will take place in a guarded laboratory cell. Use alongside people has not been established and would need a separate safety assessment.

items.title: Intelligent Robotic Hand
items.menuDescription: Sensing, edge AI and deterministic control for adaptive manipulation.
items.statusDescription: The concept and system architecture are being developed through staged technical and commercial validation.
items.summary: A modular robotic hand and forearm platform combining mechanical engineering, sensing, real-time control, computer vision and edge AI.
overview: Conventional industrial grippers perform well for repetitive tasks and predictable objects but may be less useful when shape, orientation, fragility or material changes.
The project investigates whether a modular, force-aware and vision-guided hand can provide useful flexibility without becoming impractically complex or expensive.
Development can be validated incrementally at finger, thumb, palm and integrated-hand level before committing to a complete system.
technology: Force, current, position and tactile sensing

items.title: Industrial Agentic AI Platform
items.menuDescription: A governed platform combining agents, GenAI, RAG, LLMs, tools and source-grounded QA.
items.statusDescription: This project is presented as a portfolio and future service concept rather than a completed customer deployment.
items.summary: A multilingual industrial AI platform that combines source-grounded knowledge retrieval with agentic workflows, tool use, multimodal interaction and evaluated LLM responses.
overview: Industrial organisations often store valuable knowledge across manuals, policies, reports, specifications, databases and project systems.

The platform combines modern RAG with hybrid retrieval, reranking and citations, then adds agentic orchestration so specialised agents can use tools, call APIs, coordinate tasks and preserve useful state across multi-step work.

The architecture is designed for responsible deployment with access controls, structured outputs, human approval where needed, tracing, feedback and evaluation rather than treating a fluent model response as proof of correctness.

PostgreSQL with pgvector or equivalent vector storage
Hybrid retrieval, metadata filters and reranking
Agent orchestration, tool calling and MCP-ready integrations
A2A-ready patterns for specialist agent collaboration
Tracing, evaluation, guardrails and source citation
value: Faster access to approved technical knowledge
More transparent answers with citations and evaluation
Reusable platform for internal and customer-facing AI
A controlled path from assistant prototypes to production agents

items.title: Predictive Maintenance
items.menuDescription: Machine-learning signals for equipment risk and maintenance planning.
items.statusDescription: The project requires a suitable equipment dataset and industry partner before performance claims can be made.
items.summary: A data and machine-learning system for identifying abnormal equipment behaviour and supporting maintenance decisions.
overview: Unplanned equipment failure can create downtime, cost and safety risk, but useful prediction depends on data quality and a clearly defined failure or degradation signal.
The project demonstrates how sensor histories, maintenance records and operational context can be prepared, modelled and monitored.
The system compares practical baselines with more advanced methods rather than assuming that a complex model is automatically better.

caseStudies.imageAlt: Agricultural fields and irrigation infrastructure viewed from above
caseStudies.title: Irrigation Water Quality & pH Forecasting
caseStudies.subtitle: SVM classification for acidification risk after fertiliser application
caseStudies.summary: Built a supervised machine-learning workflow from historical agricultural and environmental observations to estimate whether new irrigation-water samples were likely to become acidic.
caseStudies.challenge: An agriculture company observed that irrigation water could become more acidic after particular chemical fertilisers were applied, affecting how much land could be cultivated. Historical experimental and survey data were available and the task was to predict acidification risk for new samples.
approach: Cleaned historical data with Python, Pandas and SQL; checked missing values, inconsistent records, distributions, outliers and feature-target relationships.

Used mean or median imputation according to distribution, reviewed outliers with IQR or z-score methods without automatically deleting plausible environmental extremes, and applied feature selection including Chi-square where appropriate.
Normalised inputs, compared SVM with Random Forest and other candidate models, and used K-fold cross-validation to test stability beyond a single train/test split.
evaluation: Approximately 89% accuracy in the conservative project summary.
Confusion-matrix analysis, train/test evaluation, cross-validation and stability checks were used to reduce overfitting risk.
caseStudies.production: If productionised today, preprocessing and the model would be packaged together behind FastAPI or Flask, versioned with MLflow, containerised with Docker, tested through CI/CD and monitored for data and model drift.

caseStudies.title: Algae Biofuel Yield Prediction & Optimisation
caseStudies.subtitle: Neural-network prediction with genetic-algorithm optimisation
caseStudies.summary: Developed a model to predict biofuel yield from algae experiments and then search for operating conditions that could improve expected yield.
caseStudies.challenge: The agriculture company wanted to extract fuel from a specific alga and had laboratory data describing materials and experimental conditions. The goal was both to predict continuous fuel yield and to identify promising operating conditions.
approach: Cleaned the laboratory dataset and applied min-max scaling before neural-network training.
Used a neural network because the relationship between experimental variables and yield was strongly nonlinear.

Used a Genetic Algorithm with selection, crossover and mutation to search input combinations, separating prediction from optimisation: the neural network estimated expected yield while the GA searched for better conditions.
Compared the approach with a fuzzy-logic alternative.
evaluation: Evaluated as a regression problem using MSE, RMSE and train-validation loss trends.
The neural-network approach produced lower RMSE than the fuzzy-logic comparison recorded for the project.
The public page avoids a classification-style accuracy claim for continuous yield because MSE/RMSE are the more meaningful metrics.
caseStudies.production: A modern production version would preserve the preprocessing pipeline, track experiments and versions, expose the predictor as a service, and place optimisation runs behind controlled parameter bounds and reproducible experiment records.

caseStudies.imageAlt: Illustration of a water well, underground aquifer and water infrastructure
caseStudies.title: Water Resource, Groundwater & Operational Analytics
caseStudies.subtitle: Well-licence, water-use, operational and budget decision support
caseStudies.summary: Built analytics and visualisation workflows for farmland and groundwater management, operational reporting and budget analysis.
caseStudies.challenge: Management needed a clearer view of well licences, expiry dates, well depth, permitted water use, fines, operational records and budget performance across data held in databases, Excel workbooks and CSV files.
approach: Combined database, Excel and CSV sources; cleaned missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats; standardised fields and calculated licence status and remaining validity.
Aggregated operational data into daily and weekly summaries and validated it with range checks, duplicate checks and consistency rules.
Built Excel and Power BI reporting to highlight licences nearing expiry, water-use limits, operational issues and budget-versus-actual spending.
evaluation: Data-quality checks focused on missingness, duplicates, ranges and consistent field formats.
Daily and weekly aggregation was reconciled against source data before reporting.
Dashboards were structured around management decisions rather than isolated visualisations.
caseStudies.production: The workflow can be extended into scheduled ETL/ELT jobs, governed reporting datasets, automated licence-expiry alerts and monitored dashboards while preserving traceability back to source records.
